direction.comments: The macroscale is a fever dream, but not in a good way, as the world they created is supposed to look like a dream state, but ends up just looking AI-generated, and while it's supposed to have this mystique and hyper-realism to it, it just looks bad; the microscale is genuinely terrible as every performance is flat, every line of dialogue and piece of acting has no tone, being bland, with none of the characters having any chemistry and you genuinely just don't care about any of the characters; storytelling is non-existent because there legitimately isn't any story to tell, and what they try to tell is not interesting at all and very boring; tension is artificially built through these horror sequences, but you kind of expect and know what is going to happen, and you also just generally don't give a shit about what happens, so you don't really care about what's supposed to be scary

performance.comments: Has genuinely lost all the goodwill I gave her after Companion because she delivers one of the most bland performances I have ever seen to the point that a wet noodle gives off more personality than her; has absolutely zero chemistry with the rest of the cast
He is kinda just there for eye candy, and is aura farming the entire time with his stoic nature
Gives off line delivery akin to The Room as many of her lines feel like she is saying "your point of view is so different than mine"; has absolutely no chemistry with the cast, especially Thatcher
Her performance is genuinely porn-coded and incredibly annoying to watch; I think she should look for a different profession because she is so out of place in this movie
His character writing is honestly just very bad to the point that it bleeds into his performance because genuinely he provides nothing meaningful to the story

cast.comments: Every performance is bad and there is not a single good performance in this movie; everyone gives bland dialogue, bland line delivery, and there is no chemistry in the cast whatsoever; nobody feels like they are willing to help move this movie forward, and you don't really care about any of these characters, to where everyone I had good faith for before has lost it and is at a blank slate again

story.comments: The concept is genuinely stupid and not a good concept, and while it's trying to explore deeper themes, I just don't care enough to look into it; the plot structure is pretty linear with flashback sequences that function like an A-plot and B-plot that converge, but it's just dumb and doesn't warrant looking into any deeper messages; character writing is not good at all, feeling so forced, kind of porn-brained, and so bland and monotone that you just don't give a shit about any of the characters

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is terrible as Refn does not understand English dialogue or how people talk, making it so forced and bland that it proves Drive was a fluke because it's the only movie he didn't write, and while they try to make it seem like it is part of a dream state, it is just so poorly written it feels like a fever dream; the humor is stupid and not good; the symbolism is definitely there, but it is not good and I just don't care enough to look into it; the foreshadowing is definitely there too, but it is pretty obvious

score.comments: Genuinely good and well-written, providing an allusion to older, Golden Age Hollywood style scores that helps aid the dream state they are trying to achieve, making it genuinely the only good thing about this movie.

cinematography.comments: Has an art-house feel to it, and while the neon lighting gives his movies their signature look, it feels like he is trying to force the aesthetic he has across his movies; while they did try to force the aesthetic, it still is enjoyable to look at, at times

editing.comments: Very standard editing for an art-house movie, using a lot of fades that definitely help create the dream state aesthetic.

sound.comments: Pretty standard sound design that helps build tension, particularly in the fight scenes.

visual_effects.comments: Genuinely look AI-generated; the visual effects are so terrible that if they were actually created by artists, those artists need to find a new profession.

production_design.comments: The set design is pretty good, helping build the hyper-pop dream state aesthetic, but the blue screen production design is fucking atrocious and genuinely looks AI-generated.

makeup.comments: Very hyper-pop and model-esque, fitting the aesthetic fine, though nothing spectacular.

costumes.comments: Very fashion-forward to reflect the model and actress characters, showing off stylish dresses and costumes, though nothing spectacular.

review.pacing: Pacing was slow as hell and felt like a slog because nothing goes on in this movie; many sequences are unnecessarily long with stationary shots on faces of characters whose actors give bland performances, making the movie feel unnecessarily slow to where you could easily cut 20 to 30 minutes (or just not release the movie at all).
review.climax: The climax is not great, but at least there is stuff actually happening in it compared to the rest of the movie.
review.tone: Tonally it is very much hyper-pop and heavy on neon coloring like his other movies, but it feels so campy and bad that it makes it feel unwatchable; they try so hard to create this dream state aesthetic, but it ultimately falls flat and makes this movie feel like a fever dream; it also tries to go for a queer aesthetic that completely misses because Refn is not in that culture and does not understand it.
review.overall: Overall, 'Her Private Hell' is genuinely a very bad movie, not because of its messaging, but because of how boring it is; despite a good score and a somewhat visually pleasing aesthetic that try to create this 'dream state,' the movie completely misses the mark as it turns into a fever dream with its terrible dialogue, monotonous performances, and visual effects that genuinely look AI-generated; this movie was 2 hours I will never get back, and it makes me wonder if Drive was a fluke, making me discard all the goodwill I had for everyone involved with the project
